question: A support team must triage several thousand incoming messages a week, of which a small proportion involve genuinely difficult judgment. What is the most sensible arrangement?
options: A) Run the bulk on the fastest tier and send the cases it flags as difficult to the deepest tier.
B) Run everything on the deepest tier, so that the difficult cases are never handled by a lighter one.
C) Run everything on the fastest tier, since the difficult cases are only a small proportion.
D) Alternate between tiers message by message, so that the allowance is spread evenly over time.
correct_answers: A) Run the bulk on the fastest tier and send the cases it flags as difficult to the deepest tier.
explanations: Correct. A two-stage arrangement matches each message to the depth it needs, so volume is handled cheaply and the small hard tail still gets proper reasoning.
Incorrect. Paying the deepest tier's allowance cost on thousands of routine messages to protect a handful of hard ones is a poor trade.
Incorrect. The hard cases are usually where the cost of a mistake sits, so treating them as negligible is the expensive error.
Incorrect. Alternating assigns depth at random, which means some hard cases get the lightest treatment.
